# Adjudication Task — Chapter 43

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃43화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|스윽.
  6|
  7|날카롭게 벼린 단검이 홉 고블린의 시체를 파고들었다.
  8|
  9|체액이 튀고 고약한 냄새가 풍겼지만 손을 멈추지 않았다. 머리는 버리고, 등과 뱃가죽을 깔끔하게 도려낸 뒤 차곡차곡 쌓았다.
 10|
 11|“솜씨가 좋으시군요.”
 12|
 13|“……감사합니다.”
 14|
 15|최 팀장이다. 그의 호의 어린 목소리에 나는 죄책감을 느꼈다. 이런 사람을 상대로 그런 유치한 질투를 하다니.
 16|
 17|더군다나 이미 잊기로 마음먹은 허상까지 끄집어내서.
 18|
 19|‘사춘기도 아니고.’
 20|
 21|결국 얼굴이 벌겋게 달아오른 채로 작업을 끝마쳤다.
 22|
 23|10분 남짓이니 사체 한 구당 20초쯤 걸렸나? 빠른 속도에 슬쩍 다가온 임꺽정도 입을 벌렸다.
 24|
 25|“이야, 넌 밥 먹고 이것만 했냐?”
 26|
 27|“이 정도 하는 사람 많아요.”
 28|
 29|“많기는 무슨. 완전 전문가구만.”
 30|
 31|음. 살짝 뿌듯한데.
 32|
 33|앞에서 약간 겸손을 떨긴 했는데, 사실 임꺽정의 말대로 이 정도 속도를 내면서 깔끔하게 도축할 수 있는 헌터들은 많지 않다.
 34|
 35|“제가 손이 빠른 편이라.”
 36|
 37|학창 시절 공장 알바에, 인형 눈깔 붙이기까지 섭렵했던 나다. 어떻게 보면 헌터 일보다 먼저 시작한 게 이거란 말이지.
 38|
 39|“레이드 뛰면서도 계속했고요.”
 40|
 41|“아예 이쪽으로 방향을 튼 거야?”
 42|
 43|“아뇨. 그냥 병행했는데요. 투잡.”
 44|
 45|“투잡이요?”
 46|
 47|가만히 대화를 듣고 있던 최 팀장이 불쑥 끼어들었다.
 48|
 49|“어, 네.”
 50|
 51|“정확히 어떤?”
 52|
 53|“그냥 전투 끝나고 휴식 시간 쪼개서 작업하는 거죠.”
 54|
 55|“수당을 더 받습니까?”
 56|
 57|“그럼요. 그것도 일인데.”
 58|
 59|“그렇게 얼마나 하셨습니까?”
 60|
 61|“계속했는데요. 처음부터 지금까지 쭉.”
 62|
 63|임꺽정이 혀를 내둘렀다.
 64|
 65|“독한 놈. 난 그거 못 하겠던데.”
 66|
 67|“하다 보면 괜찮아져요. 체력 기르는 데 도움도 되고.”
 68|
 69|“목숨이 왔다 갔다 하는데 체력을 길러? 으하하. 최 팀장님, 내가 말했죠? 태경이 이 녀석처럼 악착같이 하는 놈 없을 거라고.”
 70|
 71|그런 말을 했어?
 72|
 73|“흠.”
 74|
 75|최 팀장은 대답 대신 물끄러미 나를 바라보더니 이내 돌아섰다.
 76|
 77|“작업도 끝났으니 다시 출발할까요?”
 78|
 79|저 반응은 뭘까. 어리둥절한 내게 임꺽정은 알 수 없는 웃음을 흘렸다.
 80|
 81|“열심히 해.”
 82|
 83|아니, 뭔데?
 84|
 85|
 86|
 87|* * *
 88|
 89|
 90|
 91|레이드는 순조롭게 진행됐다. 오랫동안 손발을 맞춰서 이제는 한 몸처럼 움직이는 E급 헌터들이 몬스터의 머릿수를 줄이면 최 팀장이 바통을 넘겨받았다.
 92|
 93|촤악-
 94|
 95|한 번 검을 휘두를 때마다 어김없이 터져 나오는 피 분수.
 96|
 97|나는 코앞에서 벌어지는 전투를 빠짐없이 눈에 담았다.
 98|
 99|‘확실히 잘 싸우긴 하네.’
100|
101|물론 자꾸 무림에 대한 생각이 드는 건 어쩔 수 없다.
102|
103|새벽마다 시민 공원에서 연습하는 춤 같은 동작이 아닌, 진짜 무공(武功)을 내 눈으로 직접 보고 익히기까지 했으니까.
104|
105|‘……어?’
106|
107|설마, 에이. 그래도 혹시?
108|
109|말도 안 되는 소리지만. 설마 그럴 리야 없겠지만 한 번 시도해 보는 거다.
110|
111|‘안 되겠지, 안 되겠지…… 됐으면 좋겠다.’
112|
113|조심스럽게 발을 떼려던 그 순간이었다.
114|
115|“태경 씨. 정리 부탁드립니다.”
116|
117|최 팀장의 목소리에 순간 정신이 확 든다. 내가 단단히 미쳤구나. 레이드 중에 한눈을 팔다니.
118|
119|‘정신 차리자.’
120|
121|나중에 뭘 하든 당장은 레이드가 최우선이다.
122|
123|그게 같은 팀원들에게 보이는 예의고, 내 명줄을 튼튼하게 만들어 줄 신념이다.
124|
125|“예. 갑니다!”
126|
127|나는 바람처럼 달려가 사체를 분해하기 시작했다.
128|
129|최 팀장과 임꺽정은 힘들지도 않은지 휴식 시간 내내 주변을 얼쩡거렸다.
130|
131|‘드럽게 신경 쓰이네.’
132|
133|
134|
135|* * *
136|
137|
138|
139|임꺽정은 다음 휴식 때도 어김없이 찾아왔다.
140|
141|“태경아. 너 창 잡은 지 얼마나 됐지?”
142|
143|“7년이요.”
144|
145|“이야, 그 정도면 아주 달인이네, 달인.”
146|
147|“……?”
148|
149|그다음 휴식 때도.
150|
151|“태경아. 너 훈련소 수석이었다고 했나?”
152|
153|“네. 근데 F급 중에서만 수석이라 큰 의미는 없어요.”
154|
155|“인마. 그게 대단한 거지. 나는 꼴등으로 수료했어.”
156|
157|“……형님도 대단하시네요. 그런데 저 작업 좀.”
158|
159|“아, 그래.”
160|
161|그리고 다음, 다음, 다음 휴식 시간에도.
162|
163|“태경아. 태경아. 태경아.”
164|
165|“형님. 달팽이관이 찢어진 것 같아요.”
166|
167|“너 전에 있던 길드에서 몇 년 동안 일했다고 했지?”
168|
169|“아.”
170|
171|지금이라도 마법사로 갈아타고 싶다. 저 인간 입에 침묵 마법 걸어 버리게.
172|
173|‘미치겠네.’
174|
175|방법은 하나밖에 없다. 정말 귀에서 피가 흐르기 전에 이 작업을 끝내는 것. 나는 이를 악물고 손을 놀렸다.
176|
177|서걱, 서걱, 서걱.
178|
179|“태경아.”
180|
181|살려 줘.
182|
183|근처에 앉아 있던 최 팀장에게 구조 신호를 보냈지만 그는 슬쩍 자리를 뜨는 것으로 대답을 대신했다.
184|
185|
186|
187|* * *
188|
189|
190|
191|“작업 끝났습니다.”
192|
193|나는 처음보다 묵직해진 가방을 메고 일어섰다. 홉 고블린은 아낌없이 주는 몬스터였다. 독 저항 성질을 띤 가죽과 쓸 만한 무기 몇 개. 그리고 E급 마정석도 두 개나 떨궜다.
194|
195|‘가죽 상태도 좋고, 마정석도 두 개. 이거 돈 좀 되겠는데.’
196|
197|아무래도 기여도가 가장 높은 최 팀장이 절반가량을 가져가겠지만 인원이 적으니 다른 팀원들에게도 남는 장사다.
198|
199|아, 물론 나는 제외. 계약서에 따르면 기본급 30만 원이 내가 받는 전부니까.
200|
201|‘기분 좋으면 좀 더 챙겨 주겠지. 뭐.’
202|
203|최 팀장은 꽤 후한 고용주다. 까마득한 C급 헌터면서 꼬박꼬박 존대해 주고, 성격이 좀 특이해서 그렇지 이 바닥에서 저 정도면 인격자다.
204|
205|‘그리고 믿을 수 있는 실력자고.’
206|
207|덕분에 안정적이고 빠른 속도로 여기까지 올 수 있었다.
208|
209|이제 남은 건 게이트의 마지막. 보스 존(Boss zone).
210|
211|눈앞의 이 석문을 열면 이 게이트의 보스 몬스터와 우리를 밖으로 내보내 줄 마력장이 기다리고 있을 것이다.
212|
213|“어이고, 열심히 움직였더니 배고프네.”
214|
215|“후딱 끝내고 나가서 국밥이나 먹자고. 태경아, 너도 올 거지? 그리고 최 팀장님도.”
216|
217|“전 괜찮습니다. 따로 초밥 시켜 먹게요.”
218|
219|“…….”
220|
221|보스 존을 앞에 두고 밥 얘기라니. 그 와중에 혼자 초밥 시켜 먹겠다는 인간까지 있다.
222|
223|‘이렇게 여유로워도 되는 건가.’
224|
225|물론 내가 할 소리는 아니다. 짐꾼에 중간중간 도축하는 것만으로도 하루 일당을 벌었으니까.
226|
227|새 길드에 취직할 때까지 최 팀장이 자주 불러 줬으면 소원이 없겠다. 이런 꿀 알바라면 백 번도 더 할 수 있으니까.
228|
229|“어떻게, 이제 슬슬 들어갈까요?”
230|
231|“네.”
232|
233|최 팀장의 대답에 임꺽정이 타워 실드로 석재 문을 후려쳤다.
234|
235|콰앙-!
236|
237|문이 터져 나가면서 돌가루와 먼지가 쏟아진다. 나는 팀원들을 따라 보스 존으로 진입했다.
238|
239|그리고 그곳에…….
240|
241|- 케룩.
242|
243|놈이 있었다.
244|
245|‘주술사?’
246|
247|놈을 본 순간 처음으로 떠올린 단어다.
248|
249|알 수 없는 문양이 그려진 로브. 한 손에는 말라비틀어진 지팡이를, 다른 한 손에는 예리한 단검을 든 늙은 홉 고블린.
250|
251|- 카륵. 취. 악토.
252|
253|석문이 부서지면서 큰 소리가 났음에도 아랑곳하지 않고 뭔가를 중얼거린다. 한 음절이 끝날 때마다 주변에 널브러진 시체들 위로 검은 기운이 피어올랐다.
254|
255|‘잠깐. 시체라고?’
256|
257|제대로 본 게 맞다. 제단 위에는 백 마리에 달하는 홉 고블린들이 죽어 있었다. 자세히 보니 원래대로라면 보스 존에서 우리가 상대해야 할 녀석들이다.
258|
259|‘이게 도대체 무슨.’
260|
261|처음 겪는 상황에 나를 포함한 모두가 굳어 있을 때, 최 팀장이 벼락처럼 외쳤다.
262|
263|“밖으로 나가요. 당장!”
264|
265|정체를 알 수 없는 늙은 홉 고블린이 고개를 돌린 것도 그때였다. 쩔그럭. 놈의 지팡이가 가볍게 흔들렸다.
266|
267|- 미타. 알로.
268|
269|공기가 부르르 떨렸다. 마법의 발현이다.
270|
271|“방패 뒤로!”
272|
273|탱커들이 황급히 타워 실드를 들어 올렸다. 하지만 그건 잘못된 판단이었다. 놈이 사용한 건 공격 마법이 아니었으니까.
274|
275|쿵. 쿵. 쿵!
276|
277|“뒤다! 통로가 막히고 있다!”
278|
279|“뛰어, 빨리!”
280|
281|젠장. 늦었다.
282|
283|시계를 거꾸로 돌린 것처럼 박살 났던 석문이 멀쩡하게 복구되어 있었다. 변화는 거기에서 끝나지 않았다.
284|
285|바닥에 널려 있던 돌무더기가 이중, 삼중의 벽을 쌓았고 동굴 벽면의 넝쿨이 그 위를 단단히 묶었다.
286|
287|“모두 비켜!”
288|
289|임꺽정이다. 근력 강화 스킬을 썼는지 전신의 근육이 터질 듯 부풀어 오른 그가 타워 실드를 들고 석문을 향해 돌진했다.
290|
291|“흐아아압!”
292|
293|쾅! 쩌저적!
294|
295|“……염병할.”
296|
297|임꺽정이 망연자실한 얼굴로 금이 잔뜩 간 타워 실드를 떨어트렸다. E급 헌터가 스킬까지 썼는데 뚫기는커녕 방패만 망가졌다.
298|
299|‘강화 마법?’
300|
301|그게 뭐건 간에 하나는 확실하다.
302|
303|이 정도 마법을 구사하는 저 늙은 홉 고블린은 최소 한두 단계 위의 몬스터라는 것.
304|
305|그리고…….
306|
307|쉬쉭!
308|
309|우리 중에 저놈을 상대할 사람이 존재한다는 것.
310|
311|‘도대체 언제?’
312|
313|최 팀장은 이미 놈을 향해 쇄도하고 있었다. 마치 통로가 뚫리지 않을 거라는 사실을 확신하고 있던 사람처럼.
314|
315|“바람이 깃든다. 헤이스트.”
316|
317|그의 신형이 쭉 미끄러진다. 백 미터가 넘는 거리가 순식간에 좁혀졌다. 다섯 걸음을 남겨 두고 최 팀장의 허리춤에서 검이 뽑혀 나왔다.
318|
319|쐐애액!
320|
321|C급 헌터가 전력을 다한 공격. 그러나 늙은 홉 고블린은 비릿하게 웃어 보였다.
322|
323|- 카륵. 취. 악토.
324|
325|변화는 순식간에 일어났다.
326|
327|쏴아아아.
328|
329|제단 위에 널브러져 있던 백여 구의 시체가 쪼그라들더니 모래처럼 흩어진다. 그렇게 완전히 뽑혀 나온 검은 기운이 한데 뭉쳐 최 팀장의 옆구리를 후려쳤다.
330|
331|퍼억!
332|
333|“큭.”
334|
335|빠르게 튕겨 나온 최 팀장이 일그러진 얼굴로 말했다.
336|
337|“막아야 합니다. 지금 당장.”
338|
339|“……저걸요?”
340|
341|이미 늦었다.
342|
343|불과 몇 초 전만 하더라도 유형화된 기운에 불과하던 그것은 빠르게 제 형태를 갖추고 있었다.
344|
345|3m에 달하는 거구. 터질 것 같은 근육과 어마 무시한 크기의 대검을 든 괴물로.
346|

“Let’s finish this quick and go get some gukbap.[^1] Taekyung, you’re coming too, right? You too, Team Leader Choi.”

“No, thank you. I’ll order sushi separately.”

“…”

[P108]
*Should we really be this relaxed?*

[P109]
Of course, I had no room to talk. I’d already earned a full day’s pay just by carrying luggage and butchering monsters between fights.

[P110]
Until I found a job with a new Guild, I couldn’t ask for anything more than Team Leader Choi calling me regularly. A sweet gig like this? I’d do it a hundred times over.

[P111]
“Well, shall we head in?”

[P112]
“Yes.”

[P113]
At Team Leader Choi’s answer, Im Kkeokjeong slammed his tower shield into the stone doors.

[P114]
Boom!

[P115]

[P116]
And there…

[P117]
—Keuruk.

[P118]
It stood.

[P119]
*A shaman?*

[P120]
That was the first word that came to mind.

[P121]
An old Hobgoblin wearing a robe covered in strange patterns. It held a withered staff in one hand and a sharp dagger in the other.

[P122]
—Karruk. Chwi. Akto.

[P123]
Despite the deafening crash of the doors breaking apart, it continued muttering without so much as a glance our way. With each syllable, black energy rose from the corpses scattered around it.

[P124]
*Wait. Corpses?*

[P125]
I hadn’t imagined it. Nearly a hundred dead Hobgoblins lay sprawled across the altar. Looking closer, they were the monsters we should have been fighting in the Boss Zone.

[P126]
*What the hell is going on?*

[P127]
Everyone, myself included, froze at the unfamiliar sight.

[P128]
Team Leader Choi’s voice cracked like thunder.

[P129]
“Get outside! Now!”

[P130]
At that moment, the unknown old Hobgoblin turned its head.

[P131]
Clink.

[P132]
Its staff shook lightly.

[P133]
—Mita. Allo.

[P134]
The air shuddered.

[P135]
Magic was taking form.

[P136]
“Behind the shields!”

[P137]
The tanks hurriedly raised their tower shields.

[P138]
But that was the wrong call.

[P139]
It hadn’t cast an attack spell.

[P140]
Boom. Boom. Boom!

[P141]
“Behind us! The passage is closing!”

[P142]
“Run! Hurry!”

[P143]
*Damn it. Too late.*

[P144]
As if time had been reversed, the shattered stone doors stood intact once more.

[P145]
And it didn’t stop there.

[P146]
The rubble on the floor rose into two, then three layers of walls, and vines from the cave walls wrapped around them, binding them tight.

[P147]
“Everyone, out of the way!”

[P148]
It was Im Kkeokjeong. His muscles had swollen until they looked ready to burst, probably from a Strength Enhancement Skill. Tower shield in hand, he charged straight at the stone doors.

[P149]
“Haaah!”

[P150]
Bang! Crack!

[P151]
“…Goddamn it.”

[P152]
Im Kkeokjeong dropped his heavily cracked tower shield, his face blank with disbelief. An E-rank Hunter had used a Skill and still failed to break through. All he had managed to do was wreck his shield.

[P153]
*Enhancement magic?*

[P154]
Whatever it was, one thing was certain.

[P155]
An old Hobgoblin capable of magic this powerful had to be at least one or two tiers above the monsters we had faced so far.

[P156]
And…

[P157]
Whoosh!

[P158]
There was someone among us who could fight it.

[P159]
*When did he—?*

[P160]
Team Leader Choi was already rushing toward the creature, as if he’d known from the start that we wouldn’t be able to reopen the passage.

[P161]
“The wind takes hold. Haste.”

[P162]
His body shot forward. The distance of more than a hundred meters vanished in an instant. With only five paces remaining, Team Leader Choi drew the sword at his waist.

[P163]
Whoosh!

[P164]
A full-power attack from a C-rank Hunter.

[P165]
But the old Hobgoblin merely gave him a sinister grin.

[P166]
—Karruk. Chwi. Akto.

[P167]
The change happened in an instant.

[P168]
Whoosh—

[P169]
The hundred-odd corpses sprawled across the altar shriveled, then crumbled like sand. The black energy drained from them gathered into a single mass and slammed into Team Leader Choi’s side.

[P170]
Thud!

[P171]
“Ghk.”

[P172]
Team Leader Choi was sent flying backward. His face twisted in pain.

[P173]
“We have to stop it. Right now.”

[P174]
“…That thing?”

[P175]
It was already too late.

[P176]
Only a few seconds earlier, it had been nothing more than a visible mass of energy. Now it was rapidly taking shape.

[P177]
A hulking body nearly three meters tall. Muscles swollen to the point of bursting. A monster wielding an enormous greatsword.

[P178]
“What the hell is that…?”

[P179]
Someone muttered in a daze. Like me, they had clearly never seen anything like it.

[P180]
Only Team Leader Choi knew what the creatures were.

[P181]
“A Hobgoblin Great Warrior. A C-rank Rare Monster.”

[P182]
The fact that something so huge was a Hobgoblin was shocking enough, but it was nothing compared to what came next.

[P183]
*A C-rank Rare Monster?*

[P184]
*Fuck, why is that thing showing up here?*

[P185]
Rare Monsters were creatures that appeared only infrequently within a given Gate. And since that Great Warrior was C-rank, it was something neither I nor the other team members should ever have encountered in our lives.

[P186]
…Not anymore, apparently.

[P187]
“You want us to fight that thing?”

[P188]
“Those things.”

[P189]
Team Leader Choi pointed at the old Hobgoblin.

[P190]
“A Hobgoblin Priest. Also a C-rank Rare Monster.”

[P191]
“Ah, fuck…”

[P192]
The curse slipped out before I could stop it. Im Kkeokjeong asked, his face rigid,

[P193]
“What are our chances? Give it to us straight.”

[P194]
“If we take out the Priest first, we have a chance. But to do that…”

[P195]
Boom. Boom.

[P196]
Team Leader Choi trailed off.

[P197]
The Great Warrior was coming toward us.

[P198]
One step. Then another.

[P199]
The cave floor shook.

[P200]
“We need to hold that thing back for a little while.”

[P201]
*Who does?*

[P202]
“Us?”

[P203]
“No. All of you.”

[P204]
“Kuwooooh!”

[P205]
The Great Warrior’s roar sent a stalactite crashing down from the cave ceiling.

[P206]
Team Leader Choi turned away, his expression more resolute than I had ever seen it.

[P207]
“The wind takes hold. Haste.”

[P208]
*Hey, you bastard.*

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

  1|＃43화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|스윽.
  6|
  7|날카롭게 벼린 단검이 홉 고블린의 시체를 파고들었다.
  8|
  9|체액이 튀고 고약한 냄새가 풍겼지만 손을 멈추지 않았다. 머리는 버리고, 등과 뱃가죽을 깔끔하게 도려낸 뒤 차곡차곡 쌓았다.
 10|
 11|“솜씨가 좋으시군요.”
 12|
 13|“……감사합니다.”
 14|
 15|최 팀장이다. 그의 호의 어린 목소리에 나는 죄책감을 느꼈다. 이런 사람을 상대로 그런 유치한 질투를 하다니.
 16|
 17|더군다나 이미 잊기로 마음먹은 허상까지 끄집어내서.
 18|
 19|‘사춘기도 아니고.’
 20|
 21|결국 얼굴이 벌겋게 달아오른 채로 작업을 끝마쳤다.
 22|
 23|10분 남짓이니 사체 한 구당 20초쯤 걸렸나? 빠른 속도에 슬쩍 다가온 임꺽정도 입을 벌렸다.
 24|
 25|“이야, 넌 밥 먹고 이것만 했냐?”
 26|
 27|“이 정도 하는 사람 많아요.”
 28|
 29|“많기는 무슨. 완전 전문가구만.”
 30|
 31|음. 살짝 뿌듯한데.
 32|
 33|앞에서 약간 겸손을 떨긴 했는데, 사실 임꺽정의 말대로 이 정도 속도를 내면서 깔끔하게 도축할 수 있는 헌터들은 많지 않다.
 34|
 35|“제가 손이 빠른 편이라.”
 36|
 37|학창 시절 공장 알바에, 인형 눈깔 붙이기까지 섭렵했던 나다. 어떻게 보면 헌터 일보다 먼저 시작한 게 이거란 말이지.
 38|
 39|“레이드 뛰면서도 계속했고요.”
 40|
 41|“아예 이쪽으로 방향을 튼 거야?”
 42|
 43|“아뇨. 그냥 병행했는데요. 투잡.”
 44|
 45|“투잡이요?”
 46|
 47|가만히 대화를 듣고 있던 최 팀장이 불쑥 끼어들었다.
 48|
 49|“어, 네.”
 50|
 51|“정확히 어떤?”
 52|
 53|“그냥 전투 끝나고 휴식 시간 쪼개서 작업하는 거죠.”
 54|
 55|“수당을 더 받습니까?”
 56|
 57|“그럼요. 그것도 일인데.”
 58|
 59|“그렇게 얼마나 하셨습니까?”
 60|
 61|“계속했는데요. 처음부터 지금까지 쭉.”
 62|
 63|임꺽정이 혀를 내둘렀다.
 64|
 65|“독한 놈. 난 그거 못 하겠던데.”
 66|
 67|“하다 보면 괜찮아져요. 체력 기르는 데 도움도 되고.”

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.
